subtitle: From Captive Prince to Architect of a Long Kingdom

panels.shot: epic wide of Warangal fort rising from dry plains under a burning sun
panels.action: Ganapati Deva stands in royal armor atop Warangal’s stone ramparts, gaze turned from the fort’s carved gateways toward a distant shimmer of tanks and temples on the horizon.

dialogue.text: From a prince held captive to a king who stretched his realm to the sea, Ganapati Deva turned war, water and stone into the long kingdom of the Kakatiyas.

i18n.hi: कैद हुए राजकुमार से समुद्र तक फैले राजा तक, गणपति देव ने युद्ध, पानी और पत्थर से काकतीयों का लंबा साम्राज्य रचा।

panels.shot: somber mid-shot inside a dim Yadava court, low-angle on the young prince
panels.action: A younger Ganapati Deva, wrists bound but head unbowed, stands before distant Yadava nobles in a shadowed hall, a faint light falling across his calm, hardened face.

dialogue.text: Tradition says Ganapati Deva’s reign began not on a throne, but in Yadava captivity—his power broken, his future uncertain.

i18n.hi: मान्यता है कि गणपति देव की राजगद्दी कै़द से शुरू हुई – यादवों की कै़द में, शक्ति टूटी, भविष्य धुंधला।

panels.shot: wide shot of a dusty Deccan landscape with Warangal’s fort in the distance at sunrise
panels.action: The sun rises over the plains as Warangal’s fortress walls emerge from morning mist, farmers and soldiers moving like small silhouettes against the stone.

dialogue.text: Yet by 1199, the records show him ruling from Warangal—the Kakatiya capital—where stone walls and dry fields waited for a king who must rebuild from weakness.

i18n.hi: पर 1199 तक अभिलेख उसे काकतीय राजधानी वारंगल से राज करते दिखाते हैं – पत्थर की दीवारें, सूखे खेत, और एक राजा जिसे कमजोरियों से फिर सब बनाना था।

panels.shot: close-up of the Palampet stone inscription surface, carved letters catching angled light
panels.action: A hand brushes dust off the ancient Palampet inscription, the fine, deep Telugu-Kannada letters shining under slanting light like lines of authority etched in rock.

dialogue.text: In 1213, at Palampet, an inscription of Recherla Rudra speaks proudly of loyalty, temples and service under Ganapati—revealing how others helped hold the kingdom together.

i18n.hi: 1213 में, पलमपेट की रेचेर्ला रुद्र की शिला–लेख निष्ठा, मंदिरों और सेवा पर गर्व से बोलती है – दिखाती है कि औरों ने कैसे राज्य को थामे रखा।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Ramappa Temple rising beside its tank, viewed from slightly above
panels.action: Ramappa Temple stands amid lush greenery and a broad tank, its star-shaped platform, sculpted pillars and tiered shikhara reflected in still water under monsoon clouds.

dialogue.text: Ramappa Temple at Palampet, with its fierce guardians and vast tank, shows Kakatiya power rooted not only in war, but in sacred stone and shared water.

i18n.hi: पलमपेट का रामप्पा मंदिर, उसके उग्र द्वारपालों और विशाल तालाब के साथ, दिखाता है कि काकतीय ताकत सिर्फ युद्ध नहीं, पवित्र पत्थर और साझे पानी में भी जड़ें जमाए थी।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Warangal council chamber, Ganapati seated, commanders gathered around
panels.action: Ganapati Deva sits on a simple but high-backed throne in Warangal, surrounded by chiefs and officers, listening, fingers resting on a map drawn on cloth.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions hint at a ruler who relied on men like Rudra and Jayapa: Ganapati’s strength lay in choosing, trusting and binding such commanders to his throne.

i18n.hi: शिला–लेख बताते हैं कि शासक रुद्र और जयपा जैसे पुरुषों पर टिका था – गणपति की ताकत सही सेनानायकों को चुनने, भरोसा करने और सिंहासन से बाँधने में थी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ganapati’s face as he studies a map, torches flickering
panels.action: Ganapati Deva leans forward, eyes tracing a rough coastline sketched in charcoal, the flicker of torchlight throwing sharp shadows on his determined features.

dialogue.speaker: ganapati_deva
dialogue.text: Warangal is our heart. The kingdom must learn to breathe toward the eastern sea.

i18n.hi: वारंगल हमारा दिल है। राज्य को पूर्वी समुद्र की ओर साँस लेना सीखना होगा।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye of a marching column moving from Warangal toward the coast
panels.action: A long line of Kakatiya cavalry and foot soldiers snakes across scrubland, banners fluttering, drums carried on pack animals as they move eastward under a blazing sky.

dialogue.text: By 1201, a stone record at Kanakadurga Temple near the coast bears Ganapati’s name—evidence that his authority had begun to touch the Krishna river and its trade.

i18n.hi: 1201 तक, तट के पास कनकदुर्गा मंदिर की शिला पर गणपति का नाम उकेरा गया – सबूत कि उसकी सत्ता कृष्णा नदी और उसके व्यापार को छूने लगी थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kanakadurga hill temple above the Krishna river
panels.action: The Kanakadurga temple perches on a rocky hill with the broad Krishna river flowing below, boats gliding past as priests and traders move along the riverbank.

dialogue.text: Temples like Kanakadurga and Chenna-keshava near Bapatla show coastal shrines wrapped into Kakatiya networks of gifts, land and protection, more than just trophies of conquest.

i18n.hi: कनकदुर्गा और बापटल के पास चेन्नकेशव जैसे मंदिर दिखाते हैं कि तटीय देवालय भी विजय की मात्र निशानी नहीं, दान, ज़मीन और सुरक्षा के काकतीय जाल में बंधे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a local chief receiving a copper-plate grant at a coastal temple
panels.action: A coastal chief kneels before a priest and an official, receiving a copper-plate grant, while behind them farmers, herders and merchants watch with quiet curiosity.

dialogue.text: As Cynthia Talbot observes, Ganapati’s expansion also built communities: grants to local elites, temples and tanks tied distant villages into a shared Kakatiya political world.

i18n.hi: सिंथिया टालबॉट बताती हैं, गणपति का विस्तार समुदाय भी बनाता है – स्थानीय प्रमुखों, मंदिरों और तालाबों को दान देकर दूर गाँवों को एक साझा काकतीय राजनीतिक दुनिया में जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Pakhal lake with embankments and fields around it
panels.action: An enormous tank like Pakhal stretches to the horizon, its earthen embankments lined with stone, green paddy fields and palms circling the water’s gleaming surface.

dialogue.text: Inland, great tanks such as Pakhal turned uncertain rains into steady harvests. Their scale suggests a state that invested in water so its long kingdom could endure famine and war.

i18n.hi: अंदरूनी इलाकों में पखाल जैसे विशाल तालाब अनिश्चित बारिश को स्थिर फसल में बदलते हैं। उनके पैमाने से राज्य दिखता है जो पानी में निवेश करता है ताकि उसका लंबा साम्राज्य अकाल और युद्ध झेल सके।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ganapati walking with engineers along a tank embankment at dusk
panels.action: Ganapati Deva walks along a broad embankment with village elders and builders, pointing toward sluice stones, as the evening light glows on calm water.

dialogue.text: We cannot say Ganapati’s own hands planned each tank, but his reign clearly favored water works. They became pillars of his rule, anchoring loyalty through full granaries.

i18n.hi: हम नहीं कह सकते कि हर तालाब खुद गणपति ने योजना किया, पर उसका शासन साफ़ तौर पर जल–कार्य को तरजीह देता था। भरपूर कोठारों से वफादारी बाँधकर ये उसके राज के स्तंभ बने।

panels.shot: close-up of the Ganapeshvaram inscription beside a temple pillar
panels.action: Intricately carved letters of the Ganapeshvaram inscription shine near a stone pillar, warriors in bas-relief above, a faint outline of the deity’s shrine behind.

dialogue.text: Around 1231, the Ganapeshvaram inscription of Jayapa Senani praises his campaigns and dance skills, yet places them firmly under Ganapati’s command and favor.

i18n.hi: करीब 1231 में, जयपा सेनानी के गणपेश्वरम् शिला–लेख में उसकी विजयों और नृत्य–कौशल की प्रशंसा है, पर सब गणपति की आज्ञा और कृपा के अधीन रखी गई है।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of Jayapa leading cavalry, banner of the Kakatiyas flying
panels.action: Jayapa Senani rides at the head of armored cavalry, a banner with the Kakatiya emblem streaming behind, soldiers poised but the moment frozen before battle.

dialogue.text: Men like Jayapa carried Ganapati’s authority onto battlefields and dance floors, showing a court culture where martial skill and artistic refinement both served royal prestige.

i18n.hi: जयपा जैसे सेनानी गणपति की सत्ता को रणभूमि और नृत्य–मंच तक ले जाते हैं – दिखाते हैं कि दरबार में वीरता और कला, दोनों राज–प्रतिष्ठा की सेवा करते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on a stylized figure of Rudra carved on Ramappa-like pillar
panels.action: A carved warrior figure on a temple pillar—styled as a commander—stands with sword and shield, his stance firm, framed by floral motifs and dancers.

dialogue.text: Recherla Rudra’s Palampet inscription claims he rescued his overlord and ruled as regent. Historians warn: such self-praise is power politics carved in stone, not neutral truth.

i18n.hi: रेचेर्ला रुद्र का पलमपेट शिला–लेख दावा करता है कि उसने अपने स्वामी को बचाया और राज्य–प्रतिनिधि की तरह राज किया। इतिहासकार चेतावनी देते हैं – यह आत्म–प्रशंसा पत्थर पर दर्ज शक्ति–राजनीति है, निष्पक्ष सच्चाई नहीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ganapati on the Warangal throne, flanked by chiefs including a Rudra-like figure
panels.action: Ganapati Deva sits composed on Warangal’s throne, chiefs standing on either side, one resembling a commander like Rudra, all frozen in a tense moment of shared rule.

dialogue.text: Still, these boasts suggest a period when Ganapati, recently freed and vulnerable, depended on powerful subordinates—balancing their ambition against the unity of his realm.

i18n.hi: फिर भी, ये शेखियाँ उस समय की ओर इशारा करती हैं जब हाल ही में आज़ाद हुए, कमजोर गणपति को ताकतवर सहायताकारों पर निर्भर रहना पड़ा – उनकी महत्वाकांक्षा और राज्य–एकता के बीच तौलते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Warangal fort, temples and tanks in one sweeping panorama
panels.action: From a high vantage, Warangal’s fort walls, nearby temples, city streets and distant tanks form a single landscape, with Ganapati Deva standing small but central in the foreground.

dialogue.text: By the time his long reign neared its end in 1262, Ganapati’s kingdom stretched from Warangal across Andhra toward the coast, bound by forts, shrines, tanks and a web of loyal chiefs.

i18n.hi: 1262 में उसके लंबे शासन के अंत तक, गणपति का साम्राज्य वारंगल से आंध्र पार तट तक फैल चुका था – किलों, मंदिरों, तालाबों और वफादार मुखियाओं के जाल से बंधा हुआ।

panels.shot: present-day shot of Ramappa and Pakhal landscape, dissolving into ghostly outlines of Kakatiya figures
panels.action: Modern visitors walk by Ramappa Temple and Pakhal lake, their forms overlapped by faint, ghostly outlines of Ganapati Deva, Rudra and Jayapa watching from the past.

dialogue.text: Today, we read Ganapati Deva not only in legends, but in stone and water—seeing how steady rebuilding, shared resources and careful alliances can turn crisis into a kingdom that outlives its king.

i18n.hi: आज हम गणपति देव को सिर्फ कथाओं में नहीं, पत्थर और पानी में पढ़ते हैं – देखते हैं कैसे धीरज से पुनर्निर्माण, साझा संसाधन और सोच–समझ कर गठबंधन संकट को ऐसे राज्य में बदल सकते हैं जो राजा के बाद भी टिकता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Captive Prince to Architect of a Long Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: कै़दी राजकुमार से लंबे साम्राज्य का निर्माता
